statement: RCU-style reclamation: one writer (tid 0) publishes fresh nodes through a shared pointer and retires the old ones, possibly from inside its own read-side critical section; readers enter, read the current node, and exit. A node is never reclaimed while any thread that entered before it was unlinked may still hold it (no use after free); nothing is reclaimed twice; the current node is never reclaimed; after all threads finish, drain() run alone reclaims everything retired; the object may live in non-zeroed memory; no data race; every operation returns. Not constrained: how promptly nodes are reclaimed before drain(). Premise: the epoch counter (EBITS bits) does not wrap all the way round while one thread stays inside a critical section.
contract: template<unsigned NT, unsigned EBITS> struct Epoch { void enter(int tid); void exit(int tid); void retire(int tid, int node); void drain(); };  NT threads with ids 0..NT-1; only tid 0 retires; a node passed to retire has already been unlinked; the implementation reclaims by calling the harness-provided void mocheck_free(int node). EBITS is the epoch counter width (32 in production, shrunk for verification).
instantiate: template struct Epoch<2, 2>; template struct Epoch<2, 32>;
scenario_rule: writes enough for reclamation to happen during the run (W = 2 and W = 3), a reader that re-enters, a writer that retires from inside its own pinned section, and a 2-bit-epoch scenario whose solo publishes push the epoch to 3 so the concurrent part crosses the wrap
